Guides / Resource Management

Shared Resources

Multiple processes compete for a limited pool of shared resources (operators, tools, vehicles). Each process requests resources when needed, uses them during processing, and releases them for other processes to use.

When to use this

  • Modeling operators, technicians, or vehicles shared across multiple production lines or service points
  • Analyzing resource contention and its impact on throughput and waiting time
  • Determining the minimum number of shared resources to achieve a target utilization or wait time
  • Modeling tool cribs, forklifts, or test equipment shared by multiple work centers
  • Any scenario where a finite pool of resources is the primary constraint on system throughput

Blocks

BlockLibraryLabelPurpose
CreateItem.lbrArrivalsAGenerates items for process A that will compete for shared resources
CreateItem.lbrArrivalsBGenerates items for process B that will also compete for the same shared resource pool
QueueItem.lbrQueueAHolds process A items waiting for resource availability; wait time reflects resource contention
QueueItem.lbrQueueBHolds process B items waiting for resource availability from the same pool
ActivityItem.lbrProcessAProcess A activity; requests and holds resources from the Resource Pool during processing
ActivityItem.lbrProcessBProcess B activity; competes with Process A for resources from the same Resource Pool
Resource PoolItem.lbrSharedPoolDefines the total number of available shared resources; Activity blocks request from and release to this pool
ExitItem.lbrCompletedACollects completed process A items
ExitItem.lbrCompletedBCollects completed process B items

Connections

  • ArrivalsA (ItemOut) → QueueA (ItemIn)
  • QueueA (ItemOut) → ProcessA (ItemIn)
  • ProcessA (ItemOut) → CompletedA (ItemIn)
  • ArrivalsB (ItemOut) → QueueB (ItemIn)
  • QueueB (ItemOut) → ProcessB (ItemIn)
  • ProcessB (ItemOut) → CompletedB (ItemIn)
  • SharedPool (Resource) → QueueA (Resource request)
  • SharedPool (Resource) → QueueB (Resource request)

Key parameters

BlockParameterTypicalWhat it controls
Resource PoolinitialResources2-5 (start with theoretical minimum, then increase)Total number of available shared resources. This is the key decision variable. Too few causes excessive waiting; too many wastes capacity.
QueueresourcePoolBlockId / resourcesNeededresourcePoolBlockId = ID of SharedPool, resourcesNeeded = 1Each Queue must be linked to the Resource Pool. Items wait in queue until both a downstream Activity is free AND the required number of resources are available.
Activity (ProcessA)distribution / arg1Triangular(5, 10, 20) minResource holding time. Resources are held for the entire activity duration, so longer service times mean resources are unavailable to other processes for longer.
Resource PoolallocationRuleFIFO or priority-basedRule for allocating resources when multiple queues compete. FIFO allocates to the longest-waiting request. Priority allocation favors higher-priority processes.

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to link the Queue block to the Resource Pool — in ExtendSim, the Queue block (not the Activity block) requests resources; if the Queue's resourcePoolBlockId is not set, resources are never requested and items flow through without resource constraint
  • Connecting the Resource Pool directly to the Activity block instead of to the Queue block — resources must be requested at the Queue so items wait for both server availability AND resource availability; resource request at Activity happens too late
  • Setting resourcesNeeded to a number larger than initialResources — if any process needs more resources than exist in the pool, those items will wait forever and the simulation will deadlock
  • Not including a Queue block before each Activity when using Resource Pool — without a Queue, the resource request linkage cannot be established and resources will not be properly requested or released

What to measure

  • Resource pool utilization (average fraction of resources in use)
  • Average wait time in each queue due to resource unavailability
  • Average queue length for each process (resource contention indicator)
  • Throughput of each process versus arrival rate
  • Resource allocation fairness across competing processes
